# nexus nexusdtoken add

Add a nexusd bearer token

Creates a bearer token named name with the given scopes (none by default) that expires after expires (such as 90d or 1h30m; never by default), and answers with the secret token, its tokenId, name, scopes, created and expires. The secret is returned once: it is never stored, logged or shown again, so keep it from this response. Side effects: the token is added to the host's token store and authenticates from the next request; the audit log records its name, ID, scopes and expiry, never the secret. A name already taken answers 409 conflict. A host holds at most 256 tokens, local ones included: past that the call answers 409 token-limit-reached with maxTokens. Successful token adds and removes together are limited to 10 per minute per daemon; past that the call answers 429 rate-limited with Retry-After and changes nothing. It answers 200 at once and creates no operation; an Idempotency-Key header is refused with validation-failed. Requires nexusd:admin, which is root-equivalent.

## Usage

```
nexus nexusdtoken add NAME [flags]
```

## Examples

```
  # Add a nexusd bearer token
  nexus nexusdtoken add <name>
```

## Flags

```
      --expires string        Lifetime: a Go duration such as 1h30m, or days such as 90d. Default: never expires.
      --filter stringArray    key=value, repeatable: print only objects whose dot path has this value; a repeated key matches any of its values
  -h, --help                  help for add
  -o, --output string         output format: table, json, jsonl, yaml (default table on a terminal, jsonl otherwise)
      --save-as-host string   store the returned token in the client configuration as host NAME, with the target's URL and fingerprint, and print the result without it; one target only
      --scopes stringArray    Scopes the token holds, such as containers:read or scripts:run:backup. Default none. Repeatable.
      --select strings        print only these dot paths of each object, comma-separated, such as name,properties.state; host and id are always kept
      --stdin                 read JSON Lines objects from stdin, such as another command's output, and run once per line: each binds its host and its id or name; a line without host uses the target host
      --stop-on-error         with --stdin, stop at the first line that fails
      --tag strings           target every configured host with this tag; comma-separated or repeated for any of several
      --yes                   do not ask for confirmation; required to mutate without a terminal
```

## Global flags

```
      --host string   target hosts: configured names, comma-separated, or all (default: NEXUS_HOST, then the default host)
      --verbose       log each request and response status to stderr
```
